newsitem.title: JORDAN: BBME says 1996 H1 profits up 30pct in Jordan.
newsitem.headline: BBME says 1996 H1 profits up 30pct in Jordan.

text.p: The British Bank of the Middle East said on Thursday net profits on its operations in Jordan rose to 1.5 million dinars ($2.1 million) for the first half of 1996, up 30 percent against the same period last year.

"The results are in line with our forecast about the growth in our balance sheet," said Edward Far, deputy Chief Executive Officer of the British Bank of the Middle East (BBME) in Jordan. BBME is a wholly owned unit of the HSBC Group.

A copy of BBME Jordan's half-year budget released to Reuters also showed a 17.6 percent rise in total assets to 207.3 million dinars at end of June 1996 against 176.3 million dinars in the same period last year.
Pretax profits rose to 2.61 million dinars at end of June 1996 against 2.58 million dinars the same period last year.
Jordan's British Bank of the Middle East which has 5 branches across Jordan, is the largest of Jordan's three global foreign banks.

The bank also plans to establish a foothold in Palestinian self-rule areas with a branch in Ramallah after submitting an application to the Palestinian Monetary Authority, which is currently being studied. It had a Jerusalem branch that was closed after the Six Day War in 1967.

Total deposits rose 15 percent to 177.8 million dinars at end-June 1996 from 154.9 million dinars a year before. Total lending stood at 104.56 million dinars in June 30, 1996, a 30 percent rise from 80.3 million dinars.
Total shareholders equity rose to 16.94 million dinars from 10.57 million dinars at end June 1995, the bank's balance sheet showed.
